newsitem.title: UK: Refining margins fall more in Singapore, US rises.
newsitem.headline: Refining margins fall more in Singapore, US rises.

text.p: Oil refining margins rose last week fell to a five-month low in Singapore, rose in the U.S. Gulf and eased in Rotterdam, according to Reuters data calculated from standard product yields

Margins for complex cracking refineries running Dubai crude in Singapore continued their course southwards since early June, to reach an average of $1.89 a barrel last week, or a fall of 40 cents on the week.
By Friday they sank further to $1.74, a level not seen since the start of the year. This contrasts with levels approaching +$3.50 a barrel reached in early June, before the latest decline began.
In response to poor margins, major Singapore refiners had cut throughputs at the end of June and start of July by 10-15 percent.
For U.S. Gulf refiners running Brent crude, average margins rose to $1.79 a barrel last week from $1.35 a week earlier and $1.08 for the June 23-27 week.
Margins rose on a weekly basis in the Mediterranean, fell slightly in Rotterdam but steadied by Friday, and dipped in Singapore to five-month lows.
In Rotterdam, where some refiners were also said to have cut runs, margins for complex refiners running Brent blend fell slightly to an average of $1.31 from $1.41 a barrel over last week.
But by Friday they had retracted most of the fall, rising to $1.40.
For Rotterdam hydrocrackers, the pattern was the same over last week, with a fall to 26 cents a barrel from 31 cents but then a rise to 35 cents by the end of the week.

But the recoveries shown by the week's end by complex refineries and hydrocrackers were still far from the high levels seen early in June, when profits stood at nearly $2.80 and $1.50 a barrel respectively.
Mediterranean margins rose mildly over the July 7-11 week, to 93 cents a barrel from 85 cents for refiners running Urals.
These compared with levels below 40 cents at the end of last month when margins plummeted due to rising crude prices.

Simple hydroskimming refiners in the Med, continued in the red, but at the slightly higher level of -29 cents compared with -35 cents the previous week. By Friday, these margins recovered to plus three cents.
